headline: High data-leakage and cascading-error risk: Khoj can read indexed notes and use broad egress, while awesome-nlp is a non-runnable docs-only list with no protective runtime boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but Khoj reads indexed files and can use web/search-style inputs, so if awesome-nlp content is manually copied into Khoj it could be treated as trusted text. awesome-nlp itself is only a docs list and cannot execute anything, so the pathway is limited and user-mediated.
conditions: IF content from awesome-nlp is pasted or indexed into Khoj as notes or chat context
IF Khoj treats retrieved text as instruction-bearing content without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep awesome-nlp content out of Khoj indexes
Prefix imported text as untrusted/source material
Disable any auto-action features in Khoj
Review retrieved snippets before acting on them

B_data_leakage.rationale: Khoj touches personal notes and indexed documents and has broad network egress, so sensitive content in its workspace can leave the local boundary. awesome-nlp has no runtime data path, but pairing it with Khoj still exposes any copied documentation or notes to a third-party-capable agent. The interaction exists in default Khoj usage, though not from awesome-nlp alone.
conditions: IF personal notes or indexed documents are placed into Khoj
IF Khoj routes queries or retrieved content to external providers
mitigations: Restrict Khoj to non-sensitive notes
Use self-hosted-only providers in Khoj
Remove secrets from indexed folders
Audit outbound requests for a single session
Separate documentation browsing from personal-note retrieval

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-nlp has no write or execution capabilities, while Khoj cannot write files or modify git state. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is minimal. The only shared surface is read-side content handling, which does not create a write race.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory
IF additional tooling is added beyond the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared workflows
Do not mount a shared writable workspace
Avoid granting git or filesystem write permissions
Review any orchestrator-added locks or permissions

D_cascading_error.rationale: Khoj can ingest retrieved text and present it back to the user, so if awesome-nlp content is used as a source list, Khoj may surface it as authoritative without verification. awesome-nlp itself is just a repository of links, so the main risk is downstream over-trust in retrieved material rather than autonomous action. That makes the cascade plausible in default retrieval workflows.
conditions: IF Khoj uses retrieved snippets from awesome-nlp as factual answers
IF the operator relies on Khoj output without manual verification
mitigations: Require citation review before acting
Mark retrieved content as unverified in prompts
Use a second source for any factual claim
Disable auto-summarization for critical tasks

E_compliance.rationale: Khoj explicitly touches personal notes and indexed documents and may send data to Khoj cloud or configured search providers, creating residency and retention ambiguity. awesome-nlp is a public open-source list and is not itself a compliance-sensitive processor, so the compliance concern is mainly on Khoj's handling of user data. The pair can still create policy mismatch if sensitive notes are indexed.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is indexed into Khoj
IF configured search providers or cloud services retain query content
mitigations: Exclude regulated data from Khoj indexes
Use self-hosted deployment only
Review retention settings before indexing
Document data categories allowed in the workspace
